'''Koniya Sign''' ({{Langx|ja|古仁屋手話|translit=Koniya Shuwa}}), or '''Amami Ōshima Sign''' ('''AOSL'''; {{Langx|ja|奄美大島手話|translit=Amamiōshima Shuwa|label=none}}) is a [[village sign language]], or group of languages, on [[Amami Ōshima]], the largest island in the [[Amami Islands]] of [[Japan]]. In the region of {{illm|Koniya, Kagoshima{{!}}Koniya|ja|古仁屋}} on the island, there exist a high incidence of congenital deafness, which is dominant and tends to run in a few families; moreover, the difficulty of the terrain has kept these families largely separated, so that there is extreme lexical geographical diversity across the island, and AOSL is therefore perhaps not a single language.
